answer_1.quote: The task of KG-to-Text generation consists in verbalising the content of a KG.
answer_1.outputs: natural language texts from knowledge graphs

answer_2.quote: All models were evaluated using the WebNLG-toolkit which includes the SacreBLEU implementation for BLEU, the pyter implementation for TER, and the official implementations of chrF++ and BERTScore.

answer_4.quote: We use crowd sourcing to filter out badly aligned (graph,text) pairs. We use the Potato annotation tool to create a website for annotation and Prolific to find participants for the study.
answer_4.guideline: The participants were asked to answer the following four questions: No omission. 'Looking at each element of the graph in turn, does the text express each of these elements in full (allow synonyms and aggregation)?'. No addition. 'Looking at the text, is all of its content expressed in the graph? (Allow duplication of content.)'. No unnecessary repetition. 'Is any content in the text unnecessarily repeated?'. Fluency. 'Please rate the text shown in terms of fluency on a scale of 1 to 5 where 5 is the highest (best) score.'
